Sasha — thanks, this is exactly the kind of concrete ask we like. High level proposal (attached: redwood-eval-playbook-v1.pdf):

1) Scope & targets
- Model: customer-provided 6.7B decoder (tokenizer and sample prompts provided)
- Metrics: TTFT (time to first token), p50/p95 token latency, tokens/sec steady-state, GPU utilization, and simulated per-token unit cost
- Concurrency envelope: 1–80 concurrent sessions, bursty traffic patterns (Poisson bursts + scheduled peak tests)

2) HW matrix
- A100 40GB (full GPU)
- H100 80GB (full GPU)
- L40S 48GB (full GPU)
- Representative MIG configs: A100 1/2/4-way slices, H100 2/4-way slices where applicable

3) Test plan & timeline
- Week 1 (Feb 6–9): baseline runs (single-session TTFT and steady-state throughput) on all backends
- Week 2 (Feb 12–16): concurrency scaling (10/25/50/80 concurrent sessions), prefix caching and batch tuning, gather p50/p95
- Deliverable (Feb 17): summary deck + raw CSVs (we can target mid-day to meet procurement ask)

4) Decision criteria for recommended fleet
- Latency SLO: p95 < 200ms for interactive flows, TTFT target < 120ms where possible
- Cost SLO: less than X per 1M tokens (we'll populate with exact numbers)
- Operational: MIG stability tradeoffs, preemption risk, utilization efficiency

I've copied Monica and Karthik — Monica will run the baseline bench and capture the CSVs; Karthik will model the cost curves and MIG tradeoffs. Laura will coordinate the MAP document and milestones for procurement sign-off.

If this plan looks good I will kick off the labs on Monday and share the first raw results mid-week.

Quick update from the lab (attached raw: benchmark-raw-20280215.csv). Highlights from single-session runs (6.7B decoder, sequence length 256 input / 128 decode):

- TTFT (median): A100: 98ms | H100: 72ms | L40S: 110ms
- p95 token latency (single session): A100: 145ms | H100: 112ms | L40S: 160ms
- Steady-state throughput (tokens/sec, single session): A100: 2200 | H100: 3200 | L40S: 2000
- Observations: H100 outperformed on TTFT and steady throughput for this model and sequence length. L40S lagged slightly but has better repacking density on some batch shapes.

Next steps planned for Week 2 (concurrency):
- Run 10/25/50/80 concurrent simulated sessions across each HW profile.
- Two config axes: (a) continuous batching (high batch sizes) and (b) low-latency prefix caching (small, frequent requests).
- Capture per-GPU utilization and per-request queueing times to inform MIG sizing.

Notes on MIG: A100 MIG slices reduced latency variance at low concurrency but hit throughput cliffs at >=50 concurrent sessions for this model. H100 MIG slices show better high-concurrency stability but need tuning for KV cache distribution. We'll have the complete matrix by Feb 16.

-Monica

Priam/Sasha — attached is the summary deck + the cost model (cost-model-hw-20280218.xlsx). Key takeaways from the concurrency sweep (10/25/50/80):

- H100 (full GPU): consistently best TTFT and p95 at all concurrency points. p95 at 80 conc: 180ms, TTFT median: 75ms. Throughput scales linearly to ~250k tokens/sec across 8-node cluster in our test harness.
- A100 (full GPU): good steady throughput but TTFT and p95 degrade faster under bursty, low-batch traffic. p95 at 80 conc: 245ms, TTFT median: 100ms.
- L40S (full GPU): competitive for batched jobs; p95 at 80 conc: 260ms, TTFT median: 115ms. Density benefits make it attractive for batch-heavy workloads.
- MIG tradeoffs: 4-way MIG slices on A100 provide lower per-instance cost and reduced latency variance for low-concurrency micro-bursts, but at >=50 sessions saw throughput cliffs (per-slice OOM / KV cache fragmentation). H100 2-way MIG kept better KV coherence and matched ~70% of full GPU throughput with lower cost.

Recommendation (short):
- For DataScale's mixed workload (real-time scoring + periodic large batches) we recommend a hybrid fleet: primary H100 full-GPU capacity for latency-sensitive, interactive traffic + L40S or A100 MIG-backed nodes for batch and predictable background workloads.
- Suggested initial split: 60% H100 (full) | 25% L40S (full for batch) | 15% H100 MIG (2-way) for low-cost, low-latency microservices.
- Estimated delta vs A100-only fleet: ~18% higher raw HW cost but ~32% lower end-to-end per-token cost when accounting for reduced tail latency and higher utilization for interactive flows (full cost model attached).
